newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: FOCUS-Argentina's CEI strikes media deals.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Argentina's CEI strikes media deals.

text.p: Argentina's CEI Citicorp Holdings this week may have enhanced its already strong appeal among investors by announcing two more deals in its push to be a leading media group, analysts said Thursday.

CEI's stock, which has surged 87 percent to 7.48 pesos since the beginning of 1997, has plenty of upside potential left if its venture into communications and media bear fruit, analysts said. In the wake of the recent acquisitions, at least two brokerage houses have taken note.
Merchant Bankers Asociados, an Argentine associate of Salomon Brothers, initiated coverage of CEI with a buy rating, forecasting a 35 percent upside.
ING Barings said the stock was trading at a 25 to 27 percent discount to its underlying value and targeted a share price of $8.5O in 12 months.

"CEI's outlook is very good. The acquisitions it has made look like part of a very focused, aggressive strategy, and it is threatening to convert itself into a leader in Argentine communications," Merchant Bankers analyst Andres Pitchon said.

CEI, once an industrial holding company, has moved aggressively into media in the past year. It also shares a controlling stake in Telefonica de Argentina together with Telefonica de Espana through Cointel, a holding company. About 40 percent of CEI is indirectly owned by Citibank.

Earlier this week, CEI signed a preliminary deal with Tele-Communications International Inc and Argentine broadcasting baron Eduardo Eurnekian to buy 64.5 percent of one of Argentina's largest cable television operators, Cablevision SA.
It also announced a deal to buy 33.3 percent of sports television channel Torneos y Competencias SA, which has a contract to show live league soccer matches in Argentina, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay.
CEI, which already has a 22.5 percent stake in another television channel, Multicanal, did not give financial details of the deals.
Press reports that the company had also bought 40 percent of media holding Grupo Federal de Communicaciones for $200 million were denied by CEI.
Christopher de Mattos, head of research at ABN Amro Argentina, said CEI was moving into media to take advantage of the sector's potential.
"Basically if you want to get into media in Argentina, you buy something like CEI or the telecommunications companies, but CEI is likely to be more aggressive," he said.

De Mattos suggested CEI was placing itself in a position to compete when the telecommunications market is thrown open in 2000. Acquiring a cable operator is an important step in that direction because it will enable CEI to "for instance offer rapid Internet access."
Although investment in telecommunications will sap funds from CEI, as the sector grows it offers strong cash flow in the future.

Some analysts, such as Daniel Tassan-Din, head of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Buenos Aires, said the stock's "upside has already been reflected." Indeed, the stock has risen from 6.0 pesos in just 10 days.

Tassan-Din said as CEI's recent acquisitions were of private companies it would take time to put a value to them. In addition, he said a challenge for CEI, which is run mainly by financial managers, will be to find somebody with expertise in telecommunications and media to direct strategy in the area.
